correctness.rationale: The explicit invertible map q=-log(1-y), qdot=x, gives U_c=(1-c)q+(1-2c)(exp(-q)-1)+c(exp(-2q)-1)/2. Its derivative is (1-exp(-q))(1-c(1-exp(-q))), fixing every turning point and exact barrier. On k<1 the right potential is (1-k)q+O(1) and left excursion logarithmic, proving T~2sqrt(2E)/(1-k). At k=1 the exact upper potential is (1-exp(-q))^2/2, whose Abel integral gives T~pi sqrt(2)/sqrt(1/2-E), and the outgoing qdot law proves t^2(1-y)->2 and tx->2. At k>1 the saddle q_s=log(k/(k-1)) has curvature -(k-1)/k, so T=(k/(k-1))^(1/2)log(1/(E*-E))+O(1). Energy conservation, positive lower potential and growth bounds prove no other annulus components and no finite-time escape in the stated domain. Verified symbolically by checker.py and analytic proof in RESULT.md; three numerical cases are not used as infinite proof.
